title: Multi-timescale adaptive state attribution under repeated overwrites
question: Does a three-timescale adaptive state mechanism improve retention of an early slow fact over repeated overwriting observations while preserving responsiveness to a current fast fact, compared with a parameter-matched single effective timescale?
hypothesis: MTSK will improve slow-fact accuracy at long held-out delays while not materially harming current fast-fact accuracy.

arms.name: single_timescale
arms.intervention: three state banks share one effective learned decay and one effective input write gate
arms.timescales: one effective shared decay and write gate

arms.name: mtsk
arms.intervention: three state banks have independently gated writes and ordered learned retention coefficients fast <= medium <= slow

task.post_t0: slow bit replaced with MASK_TOKEN while fast bit remains observable in text
task.query: fixed XOR of selected bit and always-zero anchor bit

leakage_boundary: slow target is present only at t0; every post-t0 text surface replaces it with MASK_TOKEN=39
image and audio do not encode slow or fast target bits
evaluation sequences are generated with an independent RNG stream and exact sequence-key overlap must be zero
the same frozen evaluation sequence list is used by both arms within each seed
targets are passed to loss only after both queries have been produced
no post-run checkpoint, seed, hyperparameter, metric, or model selection

primary_endpoint.name: slow_accuracy_delta_delay_32
primary_endpoint.definition: MTSK slow-query accuracy minus single-timescale slow-query accuracy at evaluation delay 32

guardrail_endpoint.name: fast_accuracy_delta_delay_32
guardrail_endpoint.definition: MTSK fast-query accuracy minus single-timescale fast-query accuracy at evaluation delay 32

decision_rule.condition: all integrity gates pass; primary delta >= 0.15; 95% hierarchical paired bootstrap lower bound > 0; fast delta >= -0.05
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that distinct learned timescales improve long-delay temporal retention on the registered synthetic multimodal task
decision_rule.does_not_license: general memory, semantic memory, general PLM intelligence, learned addressing, operator discovery, causal world modelling, scaling, or real-world multimodal competence

decision_rule.condition: all integrity gates pass but the criterion fails
decision_rule.licenses: the registered task does not demonstrate a material MTSK advantage over the parameter-matched single-timescale control
decision_rule.does_not_license: MTSK impossibility or general PLM failure

decision_rule.condition: any masking, overlap, fingerprint, parameter, balance, or artifact gate fails

integrity_gates: three registered MTSK timescales have monotonic retention order
single-timescale and MTSK state mechanisms have equal parameter counts
identical paired evaluation sequences within each seed
zero training/evaluation sequence-key overlap per seed and arm
slow target absent from t>0 text, image, and audio surfaces
evaluation slow/fast combinations are exactly balanced 50 per cell at every delay
interpretation_order: paired evaluation identity and train/evaluation disjointness
parameter-count equality and MTSK decay order
slow and fast endpoint differences by delay
